title: A message gone wrong
goal: Follow a story told with quotes, diye and -mIş, and use all of them yourself.

intro.text: Real stories mix all three: a quote with *demek* (*“Geliyorum.” dedi*), a quote with *diye* (*“Neredesin?” diye sordu*) and `-mIş` for what someone else said (*Geliyormuş*). In each sentence, ask who is speaking.

vocab.en: to get mixed up; to get into a muddle
to hand out, to give away

exercises.title: Yanlış anlaşılma
exercises.passage:
Cuma akşamı ev telefonu çaldı. Elif duştaydı, telefonu kardeşi Can açtı. Arayan, babaanneleriydi.

Babaanne “Haftaya cumartesi size geliyorum. Elif'e söyle, o güzel böreklerinden yapsın.” dedi. Can “Tamam.” dedi ve telefonu kapattı. Sonra da unuttu.

Akşam yemeğinde birden hatırladı. “Babaannem aradı!” diye bağırdı. “Ne dedi?” diye sordu Elif. Can biraz düşündü: “Cumartesi geliyormuş. Sana börek yapmanı söyledi.”

Ev bir anda karıştı. Babaanne yarın gelecek diye herkes hazırlığa başladı: Elif gece yarısına kadar börek yaptı, annesi evi temizledi, babası bahçeyi suladı.

Cumartesi kimse gelmedi. Akşam Elif babaannesini aradı: “Babaanne, neredesin? Seni bekledik!” Babaannesi güldü: “Ben haftaya cumartesi dedim, kızım! Bu cumartesi değil.”

Can babaannesini yanlış anlamıştı. Böreklerin hepsini komşulara dağıttılar. O günden sonra Can'a telefonu açtırmadılar, en azından babaanne arayınca.

glossary.en: all of a sudden, in no time

exercises.translation: On Friday evening the home phone rang. Elif was in the shower, so her brother Can answered. It was their grandmother. Grandma said, “I'm coming to see you on Saturday next week. Tell Elif to make some of her lovely börek.” Can said, “OK,” hung up, and then forgot all about it. At dinner he suddenly remembered. “Grandma called!” he shouted. “What did she say?” Elif asked. Can thought for a moment: “She's coming on Saturday, she says. She told you to make börek.” In no time the house was in a flurry. Because Grandma was coming the next day, everyone started getting ready: Elif made börek until midnight, her mother cleaned the house, and her father watered the garden. On Saturday nobody came. In the evening Elif called her grandmother: “Grandma, where are you? We were waiting for you!” Her grandmother laughed: “I said Saturday next week, dear! Not this Saturday.” Can had misunderstood his grandmother. They gave all the börek away to the neighbours. From that day on, they didn't let Can answer the phone, at least not when Grandma called.

questions.q: When did the grandmother say she was coming?
options: On Saturday of the following week
questions.explain: *Haftaya cumartesi*: **Saturday next week**. Can passed on only *cumartesi*.

questions.q: Why does Can say *Cumartesi geliyormuş* rather than *Cumartesi geliyor*?
options: He is passing on what someone told him
questions.explain: `-mIş` marks news heard from someone else: here, from the grandmother on the phone.

questions.q: Why did everyone start getting ready?
options: They thought the grandmother was coming the next day
questions.explain: *Babaanne yarın gelecek diye*: after a tense, *diye* gives the reason as they saw it.

questions.q: What does the last sentence say about Can?
options: They don't let him answer the phone any more
He doesn't want to answer the phone
He answers the phone all the time
questions.explain: *Can'a telefonu açtırmadılar*: the causative with a negative, **they didn't let Can answer the phone**.

reject.why: *Sormak* can't take a quote on its own: *“Neredesin?” diye sordu*.

exercises.text: Babaanne yarın gelecek ___ herkes hazırlığa başladı.
exercises.en: Everyone started getting ready because Grandma was coming the next day.
exercises.explain: After a tense, *diye* gives the reason as people saw it: **thinking that Grandma would come tomorrow**.

exercises.en: Grandma's coming on Saturday, she says.

accept: Can said, “[Okay|All right|Fine],” and hung up.
Can said, “[OK|Okay|All right|Fine],” and [hung up the phone|put the phone down].

exercises.prompt: I whispered so that the baby wouldn't wake up.

exercises.question: *Müdür toplantıya gelmenizi istiyor.* Who should come to the meeting?

why.1: The manager is the one who wants; the possessive *-niz* names who should come.

exercises.explain: *gel-me-niz-i*: the possessive *-niz* is **you**, plural or polite.

reject.why: That states it as your own knowledge. **I hear** points to `-mIş`: *davetliymişsin*.

exercises.explain: *bağır-dı-m*: the past with the **I** ending, after a quote attached with *diye*.

exercises.prompt: Öğretmen ödevi yarına kadar bitirmemizi söyledi.
accept: The teacher told us to finish the homework by tomorrow.
The teacher told us to finish our homework by tomorrow.
The teacher said (that) we [should|have to|had to|must] finish [the|our] homework by tomorrow.
The teacher told us to have [the|our] homework finished by tomorrow.

exercises.question: *Ali “Yorgunum.” dedi.* How could you pass this on without quoting him?

why.1: His own words, *yorgunum*, only work with *dedi* after them: *Ali yorgunum dedi*. Without it, pass the news on with `-mIş`.
why.2: That is a question: **is he tired, then?**

exercises.explain: `-mIş` passes on what he said, and **I** becomes **he**: *yorgun-muş*.

exercises.prompt: We spoke quietly so that the children wouldn't wake up.
accept: Biz çocuklar uyanmasın diye sessiz konuştuk.

reject.why: A purpose takes the imperative before *diye*: *uyanmasın diye*. *Uyanmayacak diye* gives a reason: **because they wouldn't wake up**.

accept: I will pass your message on to the manager.
I will pass on your message to the manager.
I will [give|pass] your message to the manager.
I will pass your message on to the [director|head teacher].
